findings.F1: In the rising profile on folds B and C, the 7-day excess return falls as the swing-scaled 20-day rise grows, which is the opposite of the tested idea. Over the cases with a positive swing-scaled rise the slope is -0.029 (t -2.41, 440 cases on 100 days). Over the upper half of those cases it is steeper, at -0.060 (t -3.59, 220 cases on 66 days).
findings.F2: The same negative grading appears at every horizon checked in the rising profile, though with fewer independent days the longer the horizon.
findings.F3: At 14 days the result depends on which grid is used, so the 14-day horizon is fragile and the reversal is better read at the shorter horizon.
findings.F4: Outside the rising profile, the swing-scaled 20-day rise grades nothing at 14 days. All five quintiles have excesses between -1.4 % and +2.8 %, and every |t| is at most 0.67.
findings.F5: In the rising profile, cases with a high swing-scaled rise also tend to have high recent agitation.
findings.F6: Neither a single day's move nor the weekday predicts anything once same-day cases are grouped.
findings.F7: The book earns mainly by riding long holds in the rising market, not from the forecast's grading.

ideas.idea: In a rising market, the more of its 20-day daily swings a coin's 20-day rise spans, the more the coin falls back against its normal drift over the next 7 days.
ideas.consequence: In an uptrend, a rise that is unusually large for the coin's own swings is a reason to refuse a fresh long, or to lean short, for the following week rather than chase it.
ideas.name: stretched uptrend rise gives back
